items.t: Turk Eximbank, QNB Türkiye sign development financing deals at COP31
sum: Eximbank secures loans totaling over $800M, while QNB Türkiye announces financing arrangements worth up to $500M

Turk Eximbank and QNB Türkiye signed financing agreements with international development institutions at the UN climate conference COP31 in Antalya, with the latter focusing on sustainable investments and inclusive growth.

Turk Eximbank signed four loan agreements with the International Bank for Reconstruction and Development (IBRD), the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank (AIIB) and German development bank KfW, according to a disclosure to Türkiye's Public Disclosure Platform.
The agreements include €209.2 million ($231.2 million) from the IBRD, €250 million from KfW and two separate loans of $200 million and $100 million from the AIIB.
Meanwhile, QNB Türkiye signed financing arrangements worth up to $500 million with five international development finance institutions, with a five-year maturity.
The institutions include the Asian Development Bank (ADB), AIIB, European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Dutch development bank FMO and International Finance Corporation (IFC).
The planned funding will support green investments, climate finance, social development, women's entrepreneurship, agriculture, forestry and the blue economy.

Gulf security indivisible, safeguarding Gulf peoples shared responsibility: Saif bin Zayed
sum: MANAMA, (Pakistan Point News - 12th Nov, 2026) H.H. Lt. General Sheikh Saif bin Zayed Al Nahyan, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, headed the UAE delegation to the 43rd meeting of the Interior Ministers of the GCC states, held in the Kingdom of Bahrain.
The meeting was attended by the interior ministers and heads of delegations of the GCC member states, as well as Jasem Mohamed Albudaiwi, Secretary-General of the GCC.
In his address, H.H. Sheikh Saif reaffirmed the common destiny of the GCC states and their firm determination to safeguard the security and stability of the Gulf, whatever the challenges may be.

Sheikh Saif further highlighted the importance of advancing security integration and aligning efforts and positions in responding to regional and international developments, in keeping with the directives of the GCC leaders. He stressed that Gulf security is indivisible and that safeguarding its achievements and protecting its peoples is a collective responsibility.

H.H. Sheikh Saif conveyed his gratitude and appreciation to the Kingdom of Bahrain and General Sheikh Rashid bin Abdullah Al Khalifa, Bahrain's Minister of Interior, for their gracious hospitality and warm welcome. He also praised the GCC General Secretariat for its efforts in supporting the successful organisation of the meeting.

Why a Zero Trust Approach Matters to Banking Resilience
sum: The principle behind zero trust is straightforward. Being inside a bank’s network does not, by itself, make a user or device trustworthy.

Dr Alex Constantinidis is group chief information security officer of QNB Group. In this contributed piece he sets out QNB’s zero trust approach and what it has taught the bank about resilience, he explains how applying that discipline for almost a decade has shaped the way the bank contains a compromise, governs what leaves its network and prepares for change.
Access must be explicitly authorised and limited to what is needed. If an account, device or application is compromised, the security architecture should help contain the consequences.

That works in two directions. Looking inward, it governs what a potentially compromised account or system can reach once inside the network. Looking outward, it governs what employees and systems are allowed to reach beyond it. Both matter, and a bank’s resilience depends on applying the same discipline to each.

At QNB Group, a zero trust approach has guided both for almost a decade. It has shaped how we design our network security architecture to contain a potential compromise, and how we govern what connects outward from it, as our digital environment has evolved. That experience offers a practical perspective on a central responsibility for banks: expanding digital capabilities while protecting the institution’s systems, its employees and, by extension, the customers who depend on it.
For us, zero trust connects everyday security decisions with the Group’s long-term resilience and ability to adapt.

An airport offers a useful way to understand layered access. Entering the terminal does not entitle a traveller to go everywhere. Identity checks, security screening and restricted zones each serve a purpose, and additional authorisation is required to pass from landside to airside.

Vietnam's Growth Continues But Will Depend On Stronger Domestic Economy's Integration: QNB
sum: Doha, Qatar: Vietnam's growth is set to continue, but its quality will depend on the domestic economy, Qatar National Bank (QNB) said in its weekly economic commentary.

The export boom remains largely captured by foreign firms, while the new wave of technology investment and stronger domestic demand offer an opportunity to deepen local linkages. Seizing it will require investment in skills, faster project execution and stronger local suppliers.

Vietnam has become one of the standout growth stories of the global economy in recent years. In the third quarter of 2026, real GDP expanded 9.95% year-on-year, the fastest quarterly pace in four years, bringing growth for the first nine months to 9.01%. This acceleration builds on an expansion of 8.02% in 2025, already the strongest performance since 2011.

The momentum has been underpinned by a historic pipeline of foreign direct investment (FDI), with registered commitments rising 76.4% to USD 50.4 Bn in the first nine months of the year, while disbursements reached their highest nine-month level in five years.
These achievements have been recognised internationally, as the World Bank reclassified Vietnam as an upper-middle-income economy in July 2026.
With the government targeting annual growth of at least 10% through 2030, Vietnam is increasingly viewed as Asia's next "tiger” economy, following the path once travelled by Korea and Taiwan.
However, a closer look at the composition of growth reveals an economy running at two speeds.

QNB Finansbank stock draws focus to Turkish banking earnings
sum: QNB Finansbank is drawing investor attention through its profitability profile and broad Turkish banking franchise. On its investor-relations page, the bank reports 2025 assets of 1.837 trillion TRY, net loans of 1.081 trillion TRY, customer deposits of 953.7 billion TRY and net profit of 47.8 billion TRY. The figures are based on bank-only financial statements prepared under Turkish banking rules.

The figures point to a large balance sheet with earnings exposure to lending, deposits and treasury activities. For investors, the key question is how effectively QNB Finansbank can preserve margins and asset quality as Turkish rates, inflation and the lira shape funding and credit conditions.

QNB Finansbank's shareholder structure is highly concentrated. The investor-relations page shows Qatar National Bank as the controlling shareholder, giving the Turkish operation access to a large international banking group while leaving minority investors exposed to the strategy and capital-allocation decisions of the parent.

Investing.com identifies the security as QNB Bank A.S., formerly QNB Finansbank A.S., with ticker QNBTR on the Istanbul Stock Exchange and ISIN TRAFINBN91N3. Its published quote page shows the last reported trading level at 157.800 TRY for November 8, 2026, with a previous close of 162.500 TRY. This is an Istanbul quotation in Turkish lira, not a euro quote on Lang & Schwarz.

QNB Bank A.S. provides retail, corporate and commercial banking, treasury and general-directorate services in Turkey. Its products include deposits, consumer and mortgage loans, credit cards, payments, insurance, investment products, cash management and financing for companies and small and medium-sized businesses. The bank is headquartered in Istanbul and is a subsidiary of Qatar National Bank.

In the Turkish banking market, QNB Finansbank competes with Garanti BBVA, VakifBank and Isbank, among others. Its position is that of a broad-based, foreign-owned Turkish bank rather than a narrowly specialized lender, while its parent-company relationship distinguishes it from the largest domestically controlled peers.
Market conditions remain important for Turkish financial shares, with investors watching inflation, monetary policy, the lira and credit quality across the banking sector.

QNB: Vietnam’s Growth Continues but Will Depend on Stronger Domestic Economy’s Integration
sum: Doha, November 07 (QNA) – Vietnam’s growth is set to continue, but its quality will depend on the domestic economy, Qatar National Bank (QNB) said in its weekly economic commentary.

The export boom remains largely captured by foreign firms, while the new wave of technology investment and stronger domestic demand offer an opportunity to deepen local linkages. Seizing it will require investment in skills, faster project execution and stronger local suppliers.

Vietnam has become one of the standout growth stories of the global economy in recent years. In the third quarter of 2026, real GDP expanded 9.95% year-on-year, the fastest quarterly pace in four years, bringing growth for the first nine months to 9.01%. This acceleration builds on an expansion of 8.02% in 2025, already the strongest performance since 2011. The momentum has been underpinned by a historic pipeline of foreign direct investment (FDI), with registered commitments rising 76.4% to USD 50.4 Bn in the first nine months of the year, while disbursements reached their highest nine-month level in five years. These achievements have been recognised internationally, as the World Bank reclassified Vietnam as an upper-middle-income economy in July 2026. With the government targeting annual growth of at least 10% through 2030, Vietnam is increasingly viewed as Asia’s next “tiger” economy, following the path once travelled by Korea and Taiwan.

However, a closer look at the composition of growth reveals an economy running at two speeds. The boom is concentrated in a foreign-owned, export-oriented manufacturing sector, as FDI firms account for most of Vietnam’s high-tech exports and of the imported components and machinery needed to produce them. Domestic firms, by contrast, remain largely confined to assembly, processing and ancillary supply activities with low value added.

This reliance on imported inputs is visible in trade data: in the first nine months of the year, imports grew 36.7%, outpacing exports at 24.5%, partly reflecting higher energy prices, with China the largest source of imports at USD 187.3 Bn.

PSG QNB WE RUN DOHA Brings 2,300 Runners to Lusail
QNB brings communities together through PSG QNB WE RUN DOHA
sum: Doha, Qatar: QNB Group, a leading financial institution in the Middle East and Africa, successfully concluded the inaugural PSG QNB WE RUN DOHA, bringing together 2,300 runners at Lusail International Circuit in a celebration of community spirit, inclusion and the unifying power of sport.

More than a running event, the initiative created a shared sporting experience for people of different ages, backgrounds and abilities, including children, families, amateur and professional runners, and participants with special needs. Organised in collaboration with Paris Saint-Germain (PSG) as part of the global PSG Running series, the event reflected a shared commitment to making sport more accessible and inclusive.

As Title Partner, QNB Group reinforced its longstanding strategic partnership with PSG, extending the collaboration beyond professional football to support grassroots participation and promote active lifestyles.

The event featured a variety of race categories designed to encourage broad participation, including 10km and 5km races for adults and a 1 km race for children. Beyond the races, dedicated children’s activities and family-friendly experiences provided opportunities for non-runners to join the celebrations.

The event was attended by H E Saad bin Ali Al Kharji, Chairman of Qatar Tourism, and H E Nasser bin Ghanem Al Khelaifi, President of Paris Saint-Germain, alongside senior executives from QNB Group. The closing ceremony recognised the winners of the men’s and women’s 5km and 10km race categories, celebrating their achievements and sporting excellence.

PSG QNB WE RUN DOHA forms part of QNB Group’s Corporate Social Responsibility strategy, which prioritises community development, inclusion and wellbeing. The initiative also supports the objectives of Qatar National Vision 2030, particularly its focus on human and social development, by encouraging healthy lifestyles and strengthening community participation.

Through its longstanding partnership with PSG and continued investment in community-focused initiatives, QNB demonstrates its commitment to being a bank for everyone, creating shared experiences that bring people together and generate positive impact beyond traditional banking services.

items.t: QNB Group confirms final allocation of shares ahead of Dandy IPO
sum: With the final share allocations having been confirmed, Dandy will now proceed with the remaining stages of its IPO. Trading in Dandy’s stock is expected to commence in November pending finalisation of its admittance to the exchange. Through the IPO, Dandy is making 40 percent of its equity available, with strong appetite already from institutional investors including insurers and private investment firms.

QNB Group acted as Lead Receiving Bank. Other receiving banks included: Ahli Bank, AlRayan Bank, The Commercial Bank, Doha Bank, Dukhan Bank, Qatar International Islamic Bank, and Qatar Islamic Bank. Maroon Capital Advisory LLC acted as the Offering and Listing Advisor.

41,200,000 shares, priced at QR5.01 have been allocated in the IPO. The total size of the offering is QR206,412,000, including the offering and listing fees. Dandy’s market capitalisation at the point of listing will be QR515,000,000.
QNB’s participation reflects its continued commitment to supporting Qatar’s economic growth and the development of its financial markets, while contributing to the country’s economic diversification.

QNB reported a $14.8 million loss, but adjusted net income was $7.2 million.
sum: Quarterly interest income after interest expense increased, while securities restructuring drove reported earnings into a loss.

QNB (NASDAQ: QNBC) reported a third-quarter 2026 net loss of $14,774,000 as securities restructuring weighed on its quarterly results. Diluted loss per share was $2.67, versus consolidated net income of $3,648,000 a year earlier. The balance sheet restructuring produced a $27,713,000 net loss before tax. Excluding restructuring and merger-related costs, adjusted net income rose to $7,207,000 from $4,058,000, with adjusted diluted earnings per share of $1.30 versus $1.09.

Net interest income increased $6,163,000 to $19,161,000, and tax-equivalent net interest margin rose to 3.25% from 2.72%. An August offering added $48,284,000 in net proceeds through issuance of 1,232,142 common shares. Results include Victory Bancorp, acquired April 1, 2026. Nine-month net loss was $8,994,000, versus net income of $10,109,000. Non-performing loans rose to $11,688,000 at September 30 from $8,793,000 at year-end, while their share of loans fell.

items.t: Emirates NBD in talks to buy HSBC's Türkiye operations to surpass QNB: Report
sum: Dubai-based Emirates NBD is in early-stage talks to acquire HSBC's operations in Türkiye, a move that would make it the country's second-largest foreign-owned lender, overtaking Gulf rival QNB Türkiye, according to the report.
The discussions are still at an early stage, and there is no guarantee they will lead to a deal, people familiar with the matter told Bloomberg.

If the talks lead to an agreement, HSBC's Turkish operations would become the latest addition to Emirates NBD's portfolio in Türkiye, building on its $2.8 billion acquisition of a 99.85% stake in DenizBank from Russia's Sberbank in 2019.

The banking group has also reshaped the leadership of DenizBank, appointing former Garanti BBVA CEO Recep Bastug as chief executive at the start of 2025 after longtime CEO Hakan Ates stepped down following 27 years at the lender.
HSBC has operated in Türkiye since 1990, offering wholesale banking, retail banking and wealth management services.
Over the past decade, however, it has significantly scaled back its retail operations to focus on corporate, commercial and wealth management businesses.
HSBC's total assets have dropped from €10.8 billion ($12.3 billion) at the end of 2012 to €4.8 billion in 2025, while its branch network has shrunk from 338 to 36.

items.t: QNB net profit surges 2% to QR4.33bn in Q1 2026
sum: Doha, Qatar: QNB Group, a leading financial institution in the Middle East and Africa (MEA) region, announced its results for the three months ended 31 March 2026.

Net profit for the three months ended 31 March 2026 reached QAR4.33 billion (USD1.19 billion), an increase of 2% compared to same period last year. Operating Income increased by 10% to reach QAR12.08 billion (USD3.32 billion) which reflects the Group’s ability to maintain successful growth across a range of revenue sources.

Total Assets as at 31 March 2026 reached QAR1,410 billion (USD387 billion) an increase of 6% from 31 March 2025 primarily driven by an 8% growth in loans and advances to reach QAR1,028 billion (USD282 billion).
Customer deposits increased by 5% to reach QAR974 billion (USD267 billion) from 31 March 2025 reflecting QNB Group’s success in diversifying its funding base.
QNB Group’s efficiency (cost to income) ratio stood at 24.1%, which is considered one of the best ratios among large financial institutions in the MEA region.

The ratio of non-performing loans to gross loans stood at 2.7% as at 31 March 2026, one of the lowest amongst financial institutions in the MEA region, reflecting the high quality of the Group’s loan book and the effective management of credit risk.
In addition, loan loss coverage ratio stood at 100%, which reflects the prudent approach adopted by the Group towards non-performing loans.

items.t: QNB’s global edge: Building the future of international banking through people and innovation
sum: Since its inception in 1964, Qatar National Bank has evolved from a pioneering financial institution into a global powerhouse, with a presence in more than 30 countries.

From its early beginnings as a modest yet forward-thinking bank in Qatar to its current role as a leading international player in the financial sector, QNB has established itself as a cornerstone of the global banking industry. Its journey encompasses innovation, resilience, and an unwavering commitment to its customers and communities.
Bridges: As the country’s first Qatari-owned commercial bank, how proud are you of QNB’s achievements?

Abdulla Mubarak Al-Khalifa: As Qatar’s first locally owned commercial bank, we take immense pride in QNB’s journey and achievements over the past six decades. What began as a national financial institution has grown into a leading bank in the Middle East and Africa.

We are proud of our strong relationships, international footprint, top-tier ratings from international rating agencies and our brand. Today, QNB Group has a strong international network with 31,000 employees in more than 28 countries across three continents.

Our strong and stable ratings from the leading agencies, including Standard & Poor’s (A+), Moody’s (Aa3) and Fitch (A+) recognize us as the highest-rated bank in Qatar and one of the most highly rated banking institutions in the GCC (Gulf Cooperation Council) and MENA (Middle East and North Africa) region.
Finally, QNB is also the Middle East and Africa’s most valuable banking brand for the 12th consecutive year, with a brand value of over $9 billion (¥1.41 trillion).
